title: Cover the refresh-token rejection paths in the auth service
summary: Adds two integration tests for the refresh-token error branches that moved into the auth service and were never re-checked, so both 401 paths are exercised and the auth service reaches full statement coverage.
motivation: The auth-service extraction (merged 2026-07-02) moved refresh_access_token()'s error branches out of the router, and their coverage has not been re-checked since — the tech-debt tracker flags it as an open audit.

included: two new integration tests against POST /api/auth/refresh in backend/tests/integration/test_refresh_token.py covering the empty-subject and unknown-user rejection paths
ticking the 're-audit auth_service.py coverage' checkbox in docs/exec-plans/tech-debt-tracker.md
excluded: any change to app/services/auth_service.py or app/auth/auth.py behavior — the audit adds tests, it does not touch the code under test
the already-covered branches: an invalid/malformed refresh token and an access token presented as a refresh token both already return 401 in existing tests
coverage work on any module other than app/services/auth_service.py

design_facts.stack: FastAPI + SQLAlchemy 2.0 async + PostgreSQL backend (Python 3.14 via uv); pytest + testcontainers integration suite mirrored in Forgejo CI

isolation_params: Backend pytest is self-contained via testcontainers (per-worker PostgreSQL) but requires Docker; on this host Docker is reachable only through the Incus instance vader-incus-docker-host — stage the repo into /tmp inside it and run pytest from the ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:python3.13-bookworm image with --network host, per the 'Docker-backed tests from worktrees' section of ~/AGENTS.md. CI has Docker natively.

work_items.title: Test the empty-subject and unknown-user refresh rejections
work_items.summary: Two integration tests that drive a validly-signed refresh token with an empty subject and one for a user missing from the database, closing the last two uncovered 401 branches in refresh_access_token.

contract.gap: refresh_access_token() in backend/app/services/auth_service.py has three 401 paths. The verify_refresh_token failure path is already covered (test_refresh_endpoint_with_invalid_token, test_refresh_endpoint_with_access_token). Two remain uncovered: the `if not token_data.username` branch (auth_service.py line 74) and the `if not user` branch (line 79). This item covers exactly those two.
contract.empty_subject_test: Craft a refresh token the app itself would accept as validly signed but that carries an empty subject: jwt.encode({"sub": "", "type": "refresh", "exp": <future>}, SECRET_KEY, algorithm=ALGORITHM) using app.auth.auth SECRET_KEY/ALGORITHM. verify_token lets it through ("" is not None and the type matches), so refresh_access_token reaches `if not token_data.username` and raises. POST /api/auth/refresh with it must return 401 and detail exactly 'Could not validate refresh token'. This is the only input shape that reaches line 74, because verify_token already rejects a missing (None) subject.
contract.unknown_user_test: Craft a validly-signed refresh token whose subject names a user absent from the database: jwt.encode({"sub": "ghost-user-<unique>", "type": "refresh", "exp": <future>}, SECRET_KEY, algorithm=ALGORITHM). token_data.username is truthy so line 73 passes; get_user_by_username returns None so refresh_access_token reaches `if not user` (line 79) and raises. POST /api/auth/refresh with it must return 401 and detail exactly 'Could not validate refresh token'. Do not create the user; the point is that the subject resolves to no row.
contract.coverage_outcome: With both tests added, app/services/auth_service.py reaches 100% statement coverage — login (success + failure), get_user_by_username, and all three refresh branches are now executed. The pytest term-missing report must list app/services/auth_service.py at 100% with no missing lines.
contract.positive_control: The coverage claim is only meaningful if it can fail: deleting either new test must drop app/services/auth_service.py below 100% and re-list the corresponding branch line (74 for the empty-subject test, 79 for the unknown-user test) in the term-missing report. State this so the check guards the branches rather than passing vacuously.
contract.reuse: Follow the existing style in backend/tests/integration/test_refresh_token.py: the `client` fixture for the request, jwt/SECRET_KEY/ALGORITHM imports already used by that module's neighbours, and the same assert shape (status_code == 401, json()['detail'] == 'Could not validate refresh token'). No new fixtures or helpers.
contract.tracker: Tick the '[ ] Re-audit auth_service.py coverage after the auth-service extraction' checkbox to '[x]' in docs/exec-plans/tech-debt-tracker.md. This is the item's own tracker entry — no other checkbox is touched.

assertions: POST /api/auth/refresh with a validly-signed refresh token carrying an empty subject returns 401 with detail 'Could not validate refresh token', exercising the `if not token_data.username` branch at auth_service.py line 74

POST /api/auth/refresh with a validly-signed refresh token whose subject names no existing user returns 401 with detail 'Could not validate refresh token', exercising the `if not user` branch at auth_service.py line 79
The pytest term coverage report shows app/services/auth_service.py at 100% with no missing lines
Removing either new test drops app/services/auth_service.py below 100% and re-lists the branch line it covered as missing (positive control)
The 're-audit auth_service.py coverage' checkbox in docs/exec-plans/tech-debt-tracker.md is ticked
